Inspired by the classic discrete-time model of nervous activity proposed by McCulloch and Pitts in 1943, a new continuous-time model, known as the McCulloch-Pitts network (MPN), has been developed for sequence learning in spiking neural networks. This model employs a localized learning rule, in which synaptic weights update solely based on the accessible information at each synapse. The model leverages the asymmetry of connections between binary neurons to effectively learn and memorize multiple temporal patterns of binary vectors, an ability similar to that of symmetric Hopfield networks for spatial patterns. Furthermore, our study reveals the model's capability to efficiently acquire sequences of up to thousands of binary items. We also show that MPNs share a direct relationship with the efficient-margin SVM algorithm, explaining their remarkable generalization performance even with minimal network parameters. Given its efficient update rule and robust sequence memorization capabilities, the MPN model offers a practical and efficient solution for sequence-based machine learning tasks in spiking neural networks.

This paper reports on the findings from the 2022 Out-Of-Vocabulary (OOV) challenge.
The competition highlighted an underinvestigated area in Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology: accurately reading previously unseen text in real-world images during model training.
The dataset compiled for the competition comprises a diverse collection of 326,385 images, encompassing 4,864,405 text instances.
To address the challenge, a distinct validation and test set was created, comprising scene text that was not present in the training data.
The competition featured two recognition tasks: a holistic approach to reading full text and a focused task involving cropped text segments.
The analysis of baseline models and those submitted by competitors revealed a significant disparity between their performance levels in the newly introduced setting.
The proposed dataset will play a crucial role in further research to enhance the development of more versatile scene text models capable of better handling the newly uncovered scenario.

A specific type of chaos expansions can effectively analyze differential equations with uncertain factors by approximating random equilibrium states associated with such equations. This study integrates principles from validated calculations to provide precise error assessments alongside findings about chaos expansions representing random equilibrium states. This approach also develops a new framework for validated tracking, which entails accurately calculating separate solution branches in a parameter-dependent system without presuming their connections. This framework is illustrated using numerical case studies.

The increased use of sensors in industrial settings has led to the widespread collection of high-dimensional data, despite this comes with its own set of difficulties. Notably, gathering sufficient information to make a decision can be challenging due to limited sensor capabilities. Moreover, industrial systems often experience failures that affect part of the system, necessitating the identification of malfunctions to contain damages and repair affected components efficiently. To address these challenges, a new method is developed that adapts to changing conditions in real-time to monitor a system's performance. This method incorporates an approach to isolate malfunctions based on the assumption that incidents occur randomly and are limited to a particular area. Moreover, a Shiryaev-Roberts type method is developed that adjusts to high-dimensional data inputs. The efficacy of this method is tested in simulations and the approach is explored theoretically to establish its validity.

We have created a detailed analysis of the origins and development of two disrupted galaxies that merged with the Milky Way's outer layers: the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus (GSE) and Wukong/LMS-1 systems. Our sophisticated computational model, designed to simulate galaxy evolution, is trained on extensive observational data, including star clusters and individual stars within these systems, to accurately predict the relative ages of stars, their composition by metal, and their movement in space. Our results reveal that GSE experienced a rapid (10 million year) period of star formation approximately 7 billion years ago, during which metal levels increased from 1/1000 to 1/5 of the Sun's, with outer regions forming earlier and hotter stars, while colder stars were formed in the core. Our predictions also match observations of metal composition in the galaxy. Enceladus may have begun forming 9 billion years ago with lower metal levels and a distinct population of older stars, and then experienced a second, more recent episode (approximately 7 billion years ago) of star formation with higher metal levels. Our model suggests this second episode could have been triggered by gas inflow or a nearby galaxy interaction. Our work indicates that our complex computational model effectively describes both GSE and ELEGA (the progenitor of Wukong/LMS-1), with predicted relationships between star formation, metal levels, and movement in space aligning with observations, and is a reliable tool for understanding disrupted

Given a profinite group G, an S[[G]]-module is a G-spectrum that fulfills certain criteria, leading to the definition of the homotopy orbit spectrum X_{hG} associated with an S[[G]]-module X. When X's constituents meet specific finiteness criteria, a homotopy orbit spectral sequence arises with an E2-term being the continuous homology of G, taking coefficients from the graded profinite \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}[[G]]-module \pi_*(X). This is demonstrated with an equivalence for certain conditions on G and Z: specifically, (Z[[G]])_{hG} is shown to be equivalent to Z in those scenarios, with supplementary methods for further investigation provided.

A major challenge in creating AI models that can automatically process and analyze visually complex documents such as invoices is acquiring a large, high-quality dataset to train these models. Our proposed approach, known as Selective Labeling, streamlines the labeling process by limiting the labels to simple "accept/reject" confirmations for model predictions made on partially annotated documents. This is paired with a specialized strategy for active learning, designed to identify and target model predictions with the highest levels of uncertainty. Our experiments on multiple document types across three different fields have shown that selective labeling can cut labeling costs by tenfold, without a noticeable decline in accuracy.

The EuS/InAs interface has gained attention due to its potential to introduce magnetic properties in this semiconductor material, making it a strong contender for the development of spintronic technologies in the II-VI family. Using a computational model that incorporates machine-learned data and density functional theory, we have investigated how varying the bonding configuration at the interface impacts the electronic structure. By examining the stable configurations of InAs doped with EuS, we identified that the electronic structure is significantly influenced by the bonding arrangement. Notably, only one configuration results in magnetic properties for InAs, with the bonding configuration also influencing the position of the InAs dipole. Our findings demonstrate the importance of accurately modeling the bonding configuration at the interface to replicate experimental results and understand the electronic structure.

A comprehensive classification system for subsets of Baire space, categorized by Borel Wadge classes, has been introduced with enhanced effectiveness. Based on Montalbán's true stage machinery, we demonstrate that the axiomatic foundation of this classification is consistent with a strong yet relatively inclusive set of principles. Our approach replaces the traditional Wadge classes with seven classes that are defined by recursive relationships and allow for a significant reduction in computation involved with class determination, from $\omega_1$-many to only seven. Additionally, the new classes have a number of desirable properties, including consistency under various axiomatic frameworks and a smooth extension to topological spaces with countable bases.

Deep, wide, and complex Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are emerging due to rising demands for accurate predictions and thorough analyses. However, they necessitate a considerable amount of computational power and time for processing. Previous studies on pruning have focused on enhancing inference efficiency, but there's been limited research on effectively decreasing training costs. Our proposed framework, ClickTrain, efficiently and accurately enables both end-to-end training and model pruning for CNNs, distinguishing itself from previous work with fine-grained architecture preservation through pattern-based pruning, precise weight estimation, and compiler-optimized calculations. As a result, ClickTrain can deploy pruned models on mobile devices without compromise in accuracy or speed. Additionally, ClickTrain can retrain pruned models with minimal impact on performance. Our experiments demonstrate the efficacy of ClickTrain, which surpasses previous pruning methods in both pruning ratio and accuracy within a specific layer, while also showing substantial time savings during the pruning and retraining process.

This research examines the properties of specific modal logics derived from noncommutative lattices by incorporating $\Box$ and $\Diamond$. A new semantics model is introduced, specifically tailored for substructural modal logics. By applying duality principles, we demonstrate that every modal logic derived from the full Lambek calculus has a Kripke model, if it adheres to a specific structural rule. Furthermore, we establish a dual relationship between certain mathematical structures, specifically modal algebras and topological Kripke spaces, utilizing a topological model developed from Priestley spaces.

The collaborations of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory and Virgo have observed the full spectrum of merging compact binaries, which comprise binary black hole, binary neutron star, and neutron star-black hole events. Combining these detections with electromagnetic radiation holds significant potential to improve our comprehension of neutron star events, particularly their dense matter state. However, electromagnetic analysis of gravitational waves necessitates the rapid identification of signals from gravitational waves in real-time. Traditional approaches struggle to achieve this at the rate expected for future detectors. In contrast, neural networks, trained on waveform templates from the LIGO Open Science Portal, successfully detect signals in real-time, achieving a signal detection accuracy equivalent to 0.97 for 250 sensitivities higher than that of current Virgo detectors. Furthermore, they can classify 90% of signals with a precision of 0.03 in mass ratios, and 0.04 in spin parameters for binary black hole events. In addition to real-time applications, these neural networks also facilitate the development of more accurate training methods, which in turn could be used for a variety of theoretical and phenomenological purposes.

A new discovery has been made regarding a gas giant exoplanet, which orbits around a star called TOI-5542 approximately every 75 days. Initially detected by the TESS satellite, the exoplanet, which has a radius similar to that of Jupiter, has been further characterized through the analysis of radial velocity data collected using the APOGEE-2 instrument. The data suggest that the exoplanet, which has an estimated mass roughly equivalent to that of Jupiter, likely formed through migration or by remaining in its original orbit rather than being a hot Jupiter. The study also provides insight into the properties of the star it orbits, which has a metal deficiency and is less massive than our sun. Further observation of the system may help better understand the physical properties of the exoplanet and the conditions necessary for the formation of planets with specific characteristics.

Sequential decision-making in operations management problems, such as those governed by constraints, can be addressed using the constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). Two main obstacles arise when attempting to solve CMDPs for the development of optimal operational strategies: they are often characterized by an extremely vast number of states and actions, as well as a difficult-to-compute transition matrix. To resolve these challenges, we develop an algorithm that combines policy iteration with subgradient ascent. We show that this approach allows the CMDP to converge to a solution at a rate proportional to $O(\log(T)/\sqrt{T})$, where T represents the number of iterations, provided that a specific condition is met. This method also offers an efficient way to reduce the dimensionality of the CMDP by exploiting its structural properties when applicable. We successfully apply our algorithm to critical problems with such a structure: multi-product inventory control and multi-class queue management, achieving results superior to state-of-art methods.

This research outlines a method for recognizing handwritten mathematical symbols when not using an actual input device, offline. The approach involves segmenting symbols accurately into over 300 categories. Since many complex mathematical symbols require both horizontal and vertical projection to be split, but certain symbols, like the square root symbol, can't be processed this way. What's more, handwritten mathematical symbols can look very similar, for example, handwritten zero and the Greek letter null. Given the numerous mathematical symbols, over 300 in total, a highly effective classifier capable of recognizing such a wide range of symbols must be developed. Initially, this study addressed the challenge of segmentation by applying the Simple Linear Iterative Clustering method. Results showed that the accuracy of the designed kNN classifier was 84% for the salient features, while 57% and 53% accuracies were achieved with the Histogram of Oriented Gradient (HOG) and Linear Binary Pattern (LBP) methods respectively for the salient features. Also, pixel intensity had an accuracy of 43% for the 66 classes considered. The use of the modified LeNet architecture achieved an accuracy of 90% for 87 classes and the SqueezeNet architecture reached an accuracy of  for 101 classes.

A geometric interpretation is provided for superconformal quantum mechanics based on a hyper-Kahler cone that has a symplectic resolution with equivariant symplectic properties. In this framework, BPS states can be represented as specific cohomology classes in twisted Dolbeault cohomology on the resolved space. The growth rates of BPS state degeneracies, specifically their indices, are connected to Euler characteristic computations in equivariant sheaf cohomology. A notable instance is when considering the Hilbert scheme of points on a 2D plane; this yields an accurate calculation of exponential BPS state degeneracy growth rates as the number of points goes to infinity. The growth characteristics serve as a theoretical prototype for the duality concept we introduced between a 7D black hole and superconformal quantum mechanics.

We examine the relationship between network architecture and disease propagation in the contact process using numerical methods. Initially, our research reveals that the disparity in epidemic behavior between homogeneous and heterogeneous networks is surprisingly small, yet the latter's complex structure can lead to a lower overall infection rate. Unlike non-clustered networks, the presence of robust community structures in the network tends to decrease the correlation between the size of an epidemic and the network's overall connectivity. However, our results also show that a high network degree does not necessarily protect a system from a large or widespread epidemic. Conversely, a network with a low average degree but characterized by robust community structures can exhibit a higher tendency to massive epidemics. Furthermore, our research investigates how different epidemic control measures affect a network with a bimodal distribution of node degrees, demonstrating that responding to an epidemic by increasing the network's overall connectivity using generic medications can be ineffective if the method does not target specific aspects of the network's topology.

Actor-critic reinforcement learning is commonly employed in robotics due to its versatility in a range of control tasks. However, its practical implementation often results in suboptimal policy outcomes. Our approach introduces ACML, a variant of actor-critic that incorporates Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for improved policy optimization. The integration of HMC's trajectory sampling technique for action exploration in actor-critic models leads to several benefits: reduced off-policy displacement, increased target coverage, and augmented exploration of the action space. The ACML architecture is composed of three key components: the actor (policy optimizer), the critic (value function estimator), and a HMC driver, which leverages the difference between the posterior distribution of actions and a hypothetical standard normal distribution as a basis for its sampling algorithm. Our experimental evaluations have demonstrated that ACML surpasses state-of-the-art actor-critic methods in a two-robot control tasks and exhibits negligible computational parity with its predecessors.

It's widely recognized that any prime number $p$ greater than or equal to $5$ can be represented as either $6k-1$ or $6k+1$. We will refer to the number $k$ that produces a given prime $p$ as the $\textbf{generator}$ of that prime. Pairs of twin primes have the unique characteristic of sharing a $\textbf{common generator}$. As a result, searching for these twin primes at the level of their respective generators makes practical sense. This paper introduces a novel strategy for verifying the $\textbf{Twin Prime Conjecture}$ by utilizing a sieving approach to extract all twin primes at their corresponding generator levels. In the context of $\omega_{p_n}$-numbers, $x$, we are referring to numbers that satisfy the condition that $6x-1$ and $6x+1$ are relatively prime to the prime $p_n$. We can demonstrate the $\textbf{Twin Prime Conjecture}$ by utilizing the average gap distance $\bar{\delta}(p_n)$ between the $\omega_{p_n}$-numbers in an indirect manner.

Autonomous navigation in multiple environments for robots faces significant challenges, particularly when dealing with varying conditions such as different surface types and obstacles in multiple settings. Our research focuses on developing a navigation system for a mobile robot that is effective in two distinct environments: laboratory settings on smooth surfaces and outdoor areas on uneven terrain. An key component of our system is the fusion of ultrasonic sensor data using a novel algorithm, which accurately determines the robot's height above the ground surface. This information is essential for identifying the robot's posture and is used alongside accumulated experience and a map of the robot's trajectory to construct a layered structure. The controller selects the most relevant experiences to guide the robot's movement, and a new variable-assisted method enhances the system's overall performance. Through extensive testing in both laboratory and outdoor environments, our system has demonstrated positive results, and the code is available online for public access.

Nereid, a satellite of Neptune that holds the distinction of being the largest outer satellite that can be spectroscopically analyzed, exhibits an irregular orbit. Our analysis focuses on Nereid's spectral characterization utilizing its reflectance spectrum between 0.8-2.4 $\mu m$, particularly in the unexplored 0.8-1.4 $\mu m$ range, as we attempt to identify the spectral absorption features that correspond to its icy composition. Our findings indicate the presence of crystalline water ice, coinciding with existing observations. Nonetheless, using simple models consisting of intimate water ice mixtures, we fail to attain a comprehensive match of absorption bands, especially considering the spectral continuum, at the wavelengths of 1.5 and 2.0 $\mu m$. This could be resolved by accounting for both crystalline and amorphous water ice, as well as taking into account the influence of sub-micron grain sizes. Furthermore, combining magnetite with components of the CM2 chondrite Murchison offers a feasible framework for understanding the spectral variations among objects like Nereid, particularly in those with neutral-sloped spectra. It's worth noting that magnetite provides a fitting explanation of Nereid's spectral continuum, eliminating the necessity of incorporating Tholin-like organic substances.
